title: Notice a repeated word
description: Notice a word a speaker or a page repeats, and say what job it might be doing.
oneStarDescription: Mark each time a chosen word appears in a short text or a short talk you may use.
twoStarDescription: Say whether the repeat emphasizes, organizes, or just fills, and mark your view as a reading.
threeStarDescription: Point to two appearances that do different work, or say they do the same work.

title: Index a notebook
description: Make an index so you can find a note by topic.
oneStarDescription: List the topics in a notebook you use and the page or date of one note for each.
twoStarDescription: Use the index to find one note without flipping at random.
threeStarDescription: Add a new note to the index the same day, or mark the index as behind.

title: Introduce a speaker in one sentence
description: Introduce a speaker with their name and why they are speaking, in one sentence.
oneStarDescription: Check how the speaker says their name and the topic.
twoStarDescription: Say one sentence with the name and the topic, then stop.
threeStarDescription: Stop talking and let them start, and correct the name at once if you misspoke.

title: Join two pieces of clay
description: Join a handle or a coil to a clay body so it holds when leather-hard.
oneStarDescription: Roughen both surfaces and use slip or water as your clay guide says.
twoStarDescription: Press the pieces together and smooth the seam.
threeStarDescription: When the clay is firmer, look at the seam and press or note a crack.

title: Keep a color code
description: Use colors to mean the same things across one page.
oneStarDescription: Write what each color means before you use it.
twoStarDescription: Use the colors only for those meanings on the page.
threeStarDescription: Find one place the color could be misread, and change it or add a word.

title: Keep a confirmation
description: Save a confirmation so you can show the time and the reference later.
oneStarDescription: Point to the date and the reference on a confirmation you received.
twoStarDescription: Put it where you can find it, without posting it publicly.
threeStarDescription: Later, show the date and reference, and cover any extra personal numbers.

title: Keep a list of questions for a visit
description: Write questions before a visit and mark which ones got answers.
oneStarDescription: Write a few questions before you go.
twoStarDescription: During or after the visit, mark which questions were answered.
threeStarDescription: Leave one question open and say where you might ask it later.

title: Keep a phrase and its situation
description: Save a phrase you heard, the situation, and whether you would use it.
oneStarDescription: Write the phrase and where you heard it.
twoStarDescription: Write who could say it and who it might offend or confuse.
threeStarDescription: Mark whether you will use it, and why.

title: Keep a source log
description: Log each source you open for one question, including the ones that did not help.
oneStarDescription: Write the question before you open a source.
twoStarDescription: Log two sources with a line on whether each helped.
threeStarDescription: Keep one source that did not answer, and say why you are not citing it.

title: Keep a tally
description: Count events with a tally someone else can check.
oneStarDescription: Make one mark for one event, and say what counts as an event.
twoStarDescription: Group marks so a later reader can count them quickly, and total them.
threeStarDescription: Count the events again, or have someone else count the marks, and fix a mismatch.

title: Label a costume piece
description: Label a costume piece with the role and where it returns.
oneStarDescription: Attach a label with the role or the wearer.
twoStarDescription: Write where it is hung when it is off.
threeStarDescription: Put it back after use and check the label is still on.

title: Label a storage box
description: Label a box with what is inside and check the label by opening it later.
oneStarDescription: Write what is in the box, specific enough to search for.
twoStarDescription: Put the label where you can read it without opening the box.
threeStarDescription: Later, find one item using the label, and correct the label if the item is not there.

title: Label a drawer of small parts
description: Sort a drawer of small parts into labeled groups.
oneStarDescription: Group similar small parts together before you label them.
twoStarDescription: Label each group with what it is, or with unknown.
threeStarDescription: Find one part from its label, and fix a label that failed.

title: Learn the order of a public ceremony
description: Learn the order of a public ceremony you may attend, and what a visitor is asked to do.
oneStarDescription: Find a program or a page from the place that lists the order.
twoStarDescription: Mark what a visitor is asked to do, such as stand, sit, or stay quiet.
threeStarDescription: If you are unsure whether visitors may join a moment, ask a host or stay seated, and say which you did.

title: Leave a pause
description: Pause on purpose in a spoken line, and say what the pause did.
oneStarDescription: Choose a place in a short text to pause.
twoStarDescription: Speak the text and hold the pause long enough that a listener notices.
threeStarDescription: Ask the listener what they thought the pause was for, and say whether that matched your aim.

title: Leave room for a note
description: Lay out a page so a person can write a note on it.
oneStarDescription: Leave a blank space and label what should be written there.
twoStarDescription: Write a typical note in the space and see whether it fits.
threeStarDescription: If it does not fit, enlarge the space or shorten the prompt.

title: Lift a box with your legs
description: Lift a light box by bending your knees, and stop if the box is too heavy.
oneStarDescription: Stand close to the box, feet stable, and bend your knees rather than rounding to grab it.
twoStarDescription: Lift it and hold it close. If it feels too heavy, put it back down.
threeStarDescription: Turn by moving your feet, not by twisting only your back, and set the box down.

title: Tell a guest what they may use
description: Tell a guest what they may use in the kitchen or the room, and what to leave.
oneStarDescription: Name the things they may use.
twoStarDescription: Name one thing you would like left alone.
threeStarDescription: Point to one thing they should not switch on, such as a hob, if it matters, without a repair lesson.

title: Listen for the downbeat
description: Point to the strong beat in a piece of music you can hear.
oneStarDescription: Tap only the beat that feels like the start of the bar.
twoStarDescription: Count along for a few bars and say where you lost it if you did.
threeStarDescription: Come back in after a pause in your tapping and meet the next strong beat.

title: Make a card that stands
description: Fold a card that stands up and carries one message.
oneStarDescription: Fold a card so it stands on a table.
twoStarDescription: Put one message on the front or the inside, where the reader will see it.
threeStarDescription: Open and close it, and fix a fold that makes it fall.

title: Make a checklist someone else can tick
description: Write a checklist another person can tick without asking what the boxes mean.
oneStarDescription: Write checks that have a visible done state.
twoStarDescription: Ask someone to tick one item and see if they do the thing or only tick the box.
threeStarDescription: Rewrite a line that was unclear so the action is visible.

title: Make a timeline from stories you were told
description: Put stories you were told on a timeline and mark what has no date.
oneStarDescription: List events people told you, with the teller.
twoStarDescription: Place only the events that have a date or a clear order.
threeStarDescription: Leave undated events off the line and say they are unordered.

title: Make a flipbook
description: Draw a flipbook in which one thing moves when the pages turn.
oneStarDescription: Draw a simple change across several pages, such as a dot moving.
twoStarDescription: Flip the pages and show that the motion reads.
threeStarDescription: Find a page where the motion jumps, redraw it, and show the smoother flip.

title: Make a landing spot for essentials
description: Choose one spot for keys or a similar essential, and use it once.
oneStarDescription: Choose a spot near the way you leave, and tell the household if they share it.
twoStarDescription: Put the item there when you come in.
threeStarDescription: Next time you leave, find it there, or fix the spot if you did not.

title: Make a legend
description: Add a legend so someone else can read the marks on your sketch.
oneStarDescription: List each mark you used and what it means.
twoStarDescription: Place the legend where it is not mistaken for part of the drawing.
threeStarDescription: Ask someone to say what one mark means, using only the legend.

title: Make a paper puppet stage
description: Make a small stage from a box so a puppet can appear and leave.
oneStarDescription: Cut an opening in a box that is big enough for the puppet.
twoStarDescription: Bring a puppet into the opening and take it out.
threeStarDescription: Show that you can still reach the puppet and that the box is not closing anyone in.

title: Make a symbol key for your notes
description: Choose a few symbols for your notes and use them the same way twice.
oneStarDescription: Write what a few symbols mean.
twoStarDescription: Use them in a real note.
threeStarDescription: Read the note later and say whether the symbols still make sense, then fix the key if not.

title: Make a pinch pot
description: Form a small pot from a ball of clay that can sit without collapsing.
oneStarDescription: Pinch a ball of clay into a hollow that sits flat.
twoStarDescription: Show a wall that is not paper-thin in one spot and thick in another, as far as you can.
threeStarDescription: Set it aside to dry as the clay's own note says, and say you are not firing it.

title: Make a rubbing of a texture
description: Make a rubbing of a texture you are allowed to touch.
oneStarDescription: Choose a texture you are allowed to touch, not a fragile object.
twoStarDescription: Hold paper still and rub until the texture shows.
threeStarDescription: Write what the surface was and where, so the rubbing is a record.

title: Make a short stop-motion
description: Move an object a little between photos so it appears to move.
oneStarDescription: Take a series of photos, moving the object a little each time.
twoStarDescription: Play the frames in order and say what action they show.
threeStarDescription: Reshoot the frame where the object jumps too far.

title: Mark a walk for someone else
description: Mark a short walk you know so another person can follow your notes.
oneStarDescription: Write the turns of a short walk, with one landmark each.
twoStarDescription: Add about how long it took you, and say it is your pace.
threeStarDescription: Ask them to follow it, or walk it from the notes yourself a day later, and fix one unclear turn.

title: Make a table of contents
description: Make a table of contents that matches the pages in a packet you assembled.
oneStarDescription: List the parts in the order they appear.
twoStarDescription: Add a page or a position for each part.
threeStarDescription: Open one part from the list and correct the list if it is wrong.

title: Choose a table you can work at
description: Choose a table for a quiet task and move if it does not work.
oneStarDescription: Before you settle, notice the noise and whether you can see your work.
twoStarDescription: Set up only the space you were given, without spreading into the aisle.
threeStarDescription: If you cannot work, move or pack up, and say why.

title: Mark a page you will return to
description: Mark a page with a note that tells your later self why to return.
oneStarDescription: Mark a page you mean to revisit.
twoStarDescription: Write a few words on why, specific enough to understand later.
threeStarDescription: Return later, use the note, and rewrite it if it did not help.

title: Match a lid to its container
description: Match lids to containers and set aside one that does not fit.
oneStarDescription: Find the lid that fits one container and close it.
twoStarDescription: Match a small set and leave no lid forced on.
threeStarDescription: Set aside a lid or a container that has no partner, and label it or say it is spare.

title: Match pairs from a wash
description: Match pairs from a wash and set aside the items that have no partner.
oneStarDescription: Find two items that belong together and say the clue.
twoStarDescription: Match the rest and put singles in one place.
threeStarDescription: Say whether a single waits for its partner or is done, and why.

title: Measure a window for a covering
description: Measure a window's width and drop and write the numbers with the unit.
oneStarDescription: Measure the width at the place the covering would sit, and write the unit.
twoStarDescription: Measure the drop in the same unit.
threeStarDescription: Say you have measurements, not a guarantee the covering will fit, until you check the product's own guide.

title: Mirror a gesture
description: Mirror a partner's slow gesture, and notice when you add a move they did not make.
oneStarDescription: Mirror a slow gesture as they do it.
twoStarDescription: Keep mirroring for a short run without adding a move.
threeStarDescription: Name one move you added or missed, and try that moment again.

title: Move a simple puppet
description: Move a simple puppet so a watcher can tell where it is looking.
oneStarDescription: Hold the puppet still and point its face at one spot.
twoStarDescription: Move it as if it speaks one line, then still it when the line ends.
threeStarDescription: Ask a watcher where it was looking, and adjust if they say the wrong place.

title: Name a boundary for a topic
description: Say that a topic is off limits for you, and what you can talk about instead.
oneStarDescription: Say which topic you will not discuss.
twoStarDescription: Offer another topic, or say you are ending the conversation.
threeStarDescription: If they return to the closed topic, restate the boundary once, and stop if they continue.
